connections.netflix.name: Netflix extension
connections.netflix.blurb: A browser extension that records every film and series you watch on Netflix, tracking your progress in real time.
connections.koreader.name: KOReader plugin
connections.koreader.blurb: A lightweight plugin for the KOReader e-reader app that records a book to your library when you mark it as finished.
connections.guide.netflix.step1: Get the extension source (download above, or clone the repository).
connections.guide.netflix.step2: Build it: run "bun install" and then "bun build.ts" in the extension folder — this produces a "dist" folder.
connections.guide.netflix.step3: In Chrome, open chrome://extensions, turn on "Developer mode", click "Load unpacked" and choose the "dist" folder.
connections.guide.netflix.step4: Open the extension popup, click "Sign in" and confirm in the tab that opens. It will then appear as the "Netflix extension" session above.
connections.guide.netflix.reloadNote: If you rebuild the extension later, click the reload icon on chrome://extensions to pick up the changes.
connections.guide.koreader.step1: Install KOReader on your e-reader if you don't have it yet (see the official guide below).
connections.guide.koreader.step2: Get the plugin folder (download above, or clone the repository).
connections.guide.koreader.step3: Copy the folder into "koreader/plugins/" on your device, keeping the name "taletrack.koplugin" — KOReader detects plugins by the ".koplugin" folder suffix.
connections.guide.koreader.step4: Restart KOReader, open Tools → TaleTrack → Sign in, and log in with the 6-digit code sent to your email. It will appear as the "KOReader" session above.

landing.sources.reader.title: KOReader plugin
landing.sources.reader.desc: Install it on your e-reader and sign in once. As you read, it sends the page you're on; if you're offline, it keeps it and sends it when you're back online.
landing.sources.reader.text: It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife. However little known the feelings or views of such a man may be on his first entering a neighbourhood, this truth is so well fixed in the minds of the surrounding families, that he is considered the rightful property of some one or other of their daughters. “My dear Mr. Bennet,” said his lady to him one day, “have you heard that Netherfield Park is let at last?” Mr. Bennet replied that he had not.

about.title: About TaleTrack
about.subtitle: A bachelor's thesis project.
about.what: TaleTrack brings the books, movies and series you read and watch together in one place. Progress is tracked automatically: a KOReader plugin sends it while you read on your e-reader, and a browser extension does it while you watch Netflix. You can also write reviews and follow your friends' activity. The code is open source and the API is public, so anyone can build their own client.
about.tfg: TaleTrack is the bachelor's thesis of {author} for the degree in Software Engineering (Grado en Ingeniería Informática del Software) at the University of Oviedo. It is a personal, non-commercial project: no ads, no analytics and no plans to monetize it.
privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.who.heading: Who I am
privacy.who.p1: TaleTrack is a personal, non-commercial project I built as my bachelor's thesis. My name is Pelayo García Varela and I'm the one responsible for your data. If you have any questions, write to me at {email}.
privacy.data.heading: What I store and why
privacy.data.p1: Only what the app needs to work:
privacy.data.i1: Your email, your username and your password (hashed), or your Google account if you sign in with it.
privacy.data.i2: Your profile photo, if you upload one.
privacy.data.i3: The books, movies and series you track, your progress, your reviews and your friends.
privacy.data.i4: The sessions you have open on each device.
privacy.data.p2: I only use it to provide the service you ask for when you sign up. There are no ads or analytics, and I never sell or share your data.
privacy.share.heading: Who it's shared with
privacy.share.p1: Your friends see your progress and reviews according to the privacy settings in your profile. Any user can find you by your username and see your photo, but never your email.
privacy.share.p2: TaleTrack also relies on these services to work:
privacy.share.i1: Amazon Web Services, which hosts the server and the database.
privacy.share.i2: Resend, which sends the app's emails.
privacy.share.i3: Google, only if you sign in with your Google account.
privacy.share.p3: They are US companies, so your data may be processed outside the European Union.
privacy.cookies.heading: Cookies
privacy.cookies.p1: I only use the cookies and browser storage the site needs to work, so I don't need to ask for your consent. There are no third-party or advertising cookies.
privacy.cookies.i1: tt-token and tt-refresh: keep you signed in.
privacy.cookies.i3: tt-theme: remembers whether you use the light or dark theme.
privacy.rights.heading: How long I keep it and your rights
privacy.rights.p1: I keep your data for as long as you have an account. From your profile you can change your username and photo or delete your account, and everything else is deleted with it.
privacy.rights.p2: If you want a copy of your data, need something corrected or anything else, write to me at {email}. And if you think I haven't handled your data properly, you can file a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency (aepd.es).
